input.summary:
Implemented the complete Task Management API with the following files:

**src/types.ts** — Shared domain types (User, Project, Task, Comment, Notification, all input shapes) and a `ServiceResult<T>` discriminated union with `ok()`/`fail()` helpers for clean error propagation without exceptions.

**src/event-bus.ts** — In-memory pub/sub singleton. Typed payload interfaces for all three events (`task.assigned`, `task.statusChanged`, `comment.added`). Subscriber errors are isolated so one bad handler can't block others. A `const Events` object eliminates magic strings.

**src/services/user-service.ts** — CRUD for users. Owns its own `Map<string, User>` store. No event publishing, no imports from other services.

**src/services/project-service.ts** — CRUD for projects plus `addMember`/`removeMember`. Idempotent add (re-adding an existing member is a no-op).

**src/services/task-service.ts** — CRUD for tasks, `changeStatus` (enforces `todo → in-progress → done` forward-only transitions via a transition table), and `assignTask`. Publishes `task.assigned` and `task.statusChanged` events to the Event Bus.

**src/services/comment-service.ts** — CRUD for comments. Accepts an enriched input (taskTitle + authorName supplied by the router) so it can publish a rich `comment.added` event without querying other services.

**src/services/notification-service.ts** — Registers Event Bus subscriptions in its constructor. Handles all three events and creates in-memory notifications. Exposes `listForUser` and `markRead`.

**src/router.ts** — Single HTTP entry point. Parses URL path/query params, reads JSON bodies, dispatches to the correct service method, and writes JSON responses. Acts as the orchestration layer — e.g., for `POST /comments` it looks up the task title and author name from their respective services before calling `commentService.createComment`.

**src/main.ts** — Creates the `http` server on port 3000 (configurable via `$PORT`) and wires it to the router.

**src/demo.ts** — Self-contained demo that starts its own server on port 3001, runs 66 assertions covering every endpoint (CRUD, member management, status transitions, assignment, comments, notifications, edge cases), and exits 0 on full pass.

All constraints satisfied: no npm runtime dependencies, no direct service-to-service calls, each service owns its own store, forward-only status transitions enforced, single HTTP entry point in the router.
